pr_title: Fix MQTT expire_after effects after reloading
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
When the MQTT sensor or binary_sensor platform are used with the `expire_after` option, a timer used to auto expire the sensor value. When reloading the MQTT integration these sensors are not clean up and influence the availability the new loaded entity.

The PR cleans up the old `sensor` and `binary_sensor` timers at reload.

After reloading the sensor's state will be restored. A new timer will be started. When a new update is received the timer will be in sync again.

This PR also fixed an error where entities that use `RestoreEntity` were tried to remove twice.

issue_context.title: MQTT timeout misbehave after reloading mqtt entities
issue_context.body:
### The problem

This issue is harder to describe preciselly or debug. But it might be not so hard to find the issue in the code.

In short:
* There are battery powered devices (Shelly H&T)
* All are configured manually in yaml as MQTT entities (see below for example)
* Entities have `expire_after` set to 86400 (24h)

Now, if I restart HA, it nothing wrong happens. Or in another words, everything works as expected indefinitely.

Once I use reload mqtt entities using HA feature `YAML configuration reloading: MANUALLY CONFIGURED MQTT DEVICED` I can expect one or more devices will turn unavailable during incoming 24-48h. It happens even to devices configured to explicitely refresh their state even without change of sensing values (for example every 6 hours)

So devices report thay are alive evey 6 hours, but HA turns them unavailable despite that. 
And for 99% it's related to reloading mqtt entities.

What is even worse, when device is unavailable, it's not turned available by next temperature reporting. Following things are able to recover:
1. HA restart
2. Reload MQTT devices (with risk any other sensors will go offline in next day
3. wait for some time (probably for device announce performed periodicaly by it self)

Obviously, setting up devices to not use `expire_after` feature solves the issue. But it also proves that there is something wrong with expiration evaluation.

Examples below  show 3 entities created from single Shelly device. From my observations, if one sensor turns unavailable, all other do the same. But it might be because the same expiration time.

Not sure when exactly I experienced this issue for the first ime. But for sure I started be aware about it in year 2021.
If my memory serves well, the feature of reloading mqtt entities has been implemented around begining of 2021.

Here is extracted log from core and mqtt components set to debug logging. Below you can find short description.
Dates are from Nov'21 - I took it from forum post. Today I found time to report it since the issue hit me again... after I reloaded entities yesterday.

```
cat ./home-assistant.log | grep -E "temp-kitchen|kitchen_temperature" | grep -v table
```

Description to above:
at 2:28 most recent temperature value has been received from mqtt and set in entity
at 11:04 for some reason this sensor has been refreshed with the same values
at 12:51 temperature sensor went unavailable,
at 14:19 temperature is set to valid value because is refreshed from mqtt
at 14:21 it turns unavailable again without reason
at 14:25 temperature is set to valid value because is refreshed from mqtt
at 14:27 it turns unavailable again without reason
Reason of next sensor updates are not known for me but are executed roughly every 3 minutes not changing the state.

Hey there @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`mqtt`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L572) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I found another related behavior confirms that there is something wrong with expiration time when reloading mqtt entities.

At some point I decided to remove expiration time from my entities for obvious reasons.
I removed suitable lines from yaml, then  reloaded entities. 

After a day, two of my sensors turned unavailable.
I restarted HA, and have seen no unavailable entitles anymore.

It looks like reloading mqtt entities not only breaks expiration while defined, but is not able to properly disable this feature when this setting is removed from mqtt entity.

This could possibly be related to MQTTAvailability's fget failing because it's the first check in the available property.  If that fget fails, the device will fail forever it seems.  Maybe look towards the reload process and that dictionary after the reload occurs.  Might be an order of operations thing.

the `expire_after` setting will set a timer that will make the entity unavailable if no update is received. When there is a reload the timer seems to be still active. It should be cleaned up because a reload will initiate a new timer.

UPDATED!
The linked PR will:
- cleanup timers for the exiting entries using the `expire_after` option.
- restore entities and expire trigger to be available for the remaining time until an update is received.
I'll work on a recovery of the last state after a reload. UPDATE: Fixed state restore.

Great job, thank you!

> The linked PR will:
> * cause the loaded entities to be unavailable at reload until an update is received.
>   I can image it would be desirable to have entities recovered after a reload, but this fix will at least recover the sensors at the first update received.

Wonder if state 'unknown' isn't better fitting than 'unavailable' (?)
BTW I assume that if source mqtt value is retained than it will be reloaded immediately.
We improved the PR, so it will restore entities that have not expired yet. I updated the description above to avoid misunderstanding.

review_comments: For the record: This fixes an old bug which surfaced due to changed timing when `MqttSensor` and `MqttBinarySensor` extend `RestoreEntity`
The bug fix also applies for other platforms like MqttSwitch
